subject: Private hostchain TLS orchestration and routing for VPC-hosted endpoints

Subject: Private host TLS requirements: can we do a 'hostchain' handoff?

Hi David,

Thanks for taking a look. We're evaluating Redwood Private for a VPC-hosted deployment where our customers host an internal proxy (bastion) in front of Redwood's private endpoint. Our main asks are:

- We need a pattern that allows the customer to own the public/private FQDNs while still letting Redwood rotate server certs without customer downtime.
- We prefer TLS termination at the customer's bastion in some regions (for packet inspection), but want Redwood to present a valid certificate to the service endpoints in others.
- We need guidance on SNI mapping, OCSP/CRL expectations, and how to prove CSR ownership during onboarding.

Attached a short PDF with our environment sketch. Can your team propose an operational model and minimal handshake steps? Also curious about mutual TLS vs one-way TLS tradeoffs here.

Thanks,
Jules Martin
Head of Cloud Engineering
Acme Financial

Attachment: hostchain-ask-20260902.pdf (1 page PDF — environment sketch)
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>

Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private host TLS requirements: can we do a 'hostchain' handoff?

Hi Jules — appreciate the sketch and context. High-level recommendation below (we've been calling it the 'hostchain' handoff internally):

1) Ownership model: customer owns the authoritative FQDNs in their DNS and delegates a narrow SRV/CNAME (or a set of A records) for Redwood's ingress within the VPC. This preserves customer control of names while giving Redwood stable endpoints to connect to.

2) TLS termination options (per-region):
   - Customer-terminated: Bastion terminates TLS and forwards plain (or mTLS) traffic to Redwood via an internal ALB. Good when customer needs inspection or DLP.
   - Redwood-terminated: Bastion performs TCP proxying only (SNI passthrough) and Redwood terminates TLS close to the model runtime. This reduces client certificate footprint and simplifies key rotation on the customer side.

3) Certificate handoff and proof of ownership:
   - Preferred: Customer supplies a CSR for the delegated hostnames that Redwood signs (or we accept a cert chain from customer's CA). We require proof-of-control by either: (a) a DNS TXT challenge on the delegated subdomain, or (b) a signed assertion from the customer's KMS (if using HSM-backed CA).
   - Alternative: ACME flow with split-horizon DNS — Redwood will issue/renew certs for the delegated record only after DNS proof.

4) SNI and routing: Redwood will map SNI to tenant routing keys. If the bastion terminates TLS, the bastion must present a client cert (optional mTLS) that Redwood validates against a customer CA bundle. If SNI passthrough is used, ensure the customer's LB preserves the TLS ClientHello (some LBs rewrite SNI).

5) OCSP/CRL expectations: prefer OCSP stapling from Redwood when we terminate; for customer-terminated options: Redwood will perform OCSP checks on upstream certs and cache short TTLs. 

6) Operational concerns: rotation windows (target 48–72 hour rollouts), canary routing for cert swaps, and fallback to a Redwood-managed variant if we detect handshake failures.

Next steps: I'll draft a one-page operability checklist + runbook. Marissa — can you own the runbook template and list the required logs we need to capture for audit? Karthik — can you detail the SNI mapping behavior and a sample nginx/haproxy config for our docs?

Happy to hop on a 30m call if you want to walk the flow.

—David
David Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private host TLS requirements: can we do a 'hostchain' handoff? — technical notes

Quick technical notes and a config snippet to make this concrete. Attach: csr-sample.txt (CSR example for delegated hostnames).

- SNI behavior: If customer does TLS termination at the bastion, they must provide Redwood either (A) a client certificate chain for mTLS, or (B) a header-enriched TCP proxy that sets X-Forwarded-SNI. We prefer (A) for auth, but (B) is common for legacy LBs.

- OCSP/Stapling: If Redwood terminates, we will staple OCSP responses. Please ensure your bastion accepts TLS connections with TLS1.3 and allows TLS extensions for status_request (so stapling can be negotiated).

- Split-horizon DNS: For ACME flows in private zones, ensure the delegated subdomain resolves to the internal ALB inside your VPC. We will verify TXT challenges from a worker inside the VPC (we can coordinate ephemeral worker IPs if needed).

- Example HAProxy snippet (SNI passthrough):
  frontend ft_tls_tcp
      mode tcp
      bind :443
      tcp-request inspect-delay 5s
      tcp-request content accept if { req_ssl_hello_type 1 }
      use_backend bk_redwood if { req_ssl_sni -i api.acme.internal }

  backend bk_redwood
      mode tcp
      server redwood-1 10.0.12.31:8443 check send-proxy

- TTL/Cache: For delegated DNS records we recommend low TTLs (60–300s) during handoff windows, then raise to 300–900s for steady state.

Let me know if you want a pod-level script to validate SNI passthrough (I can push to the shared Drive).

—Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Jules — thanks, this is actionable and we can deliver a concise runbook. Summary of the rollout plan and deliverables below: 

1) Deliverables by EOW (initial draft):
   - Delegation doc + DNS snippet (Marissa) — responsible: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
   - CSR template + proof-of-control checklist (Karthik) — responsible: k.iyer@redwood.ai (attached)
   - Onboarding runbook (Stephanie) — responsible: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai (I attached the runbook template)

2) Rollout steps (high level):
   - Onboarding call: validate DNS delegation and obtain CSR proof (15–30m)
   - Canary: Route 10% traffic to new cert for 24 hours; watch handshake error rate and latency
   - Full swap: 100% route after 24h if no errors; keep old cert as fallback for 72h

3) Telemetry & alarms:
   - SNI mismatch rate > 0.5% in canary window -> automated rollback
   - OCSP failure rate > 2% -> alert to infra-oncall and require manual intervention

4) Meeting & next steps: I scheduled a 30m sync (Calendar link: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=example) for Mon 2026-09-07 10:00 PT to walk the draft runbook.
